title: WPMS/2107/2023 of SOBAN SINGH RAWAT Vs DISTRICT MAGISTRATE CHAMPAWAT

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No.2107 of 2023
Soban Singh Rawat ....Petitioner
Versus

District Magistrate Champawat and Others ....Respondent
Present:-
Ms. Sangeeta Adhikari Patni, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing Counsel for the State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 By means of the instant petition, the petitioner
seeks the following reliefs:-
 "(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to conduct fair
and impartial inquiry on the complaints
of petitioner and his family regarding
encroachment over their land/approach
road and to take suitable action for
removal of the encroachment done by
private respondent and further punitive
action also be taken against private
respondent for encroachment done by
him.

2
 (ii) Any other order or direction which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in
the circumstances of the case.
 (iii) Award cost of the petition."

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he is owner in
possession of a piece of land, but the respondent no.4 is
encroaching over the approach road of the petitioner
constructed on his private land. According to the petitioner,
he made various representations, but no action has been
taken.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that, in fact, the respondent no.4 is encroaching on the
pathway; various complaints have been made, but no action
has been taken.
5. The Court invited attention of the learned
counsel for the petitioner to a report dated 12.05.2023, which
has been filed along with the petition, though no annexure
has been marked on it, but it is Page No. 55 of the record.
This is a report of Tehsildar, Lohaghat, which certifies that, in
fact, the respondent no.4 has not encroached any land.

3
6. On it, learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that earlier, a compromise was recorded in which the
respondent no.4 had agreed that he would not obstruct the
pathway. .
6. Learned State Counsel would submit that it is a
dispute with regard to a private land between two private
individuals; it is a private dispute.
7. In Para 11 of the petition, the petitioner has
categorically stated that the encroachment has been done on
private pathway of the petitioner. It is the case that it has
been done by the respondent no.4, Man Singh. Petitioner is,
in fact, ventilating his grievance, which is a private law
remedy. Petitioner may very well be advised to approach the
Civil court for this purpose.
8. Whether there is encroachment or not? If so,to
what extent? Or on whose land? These are questions of fact,
which may require deeper examination of the issue on facts
or may be on law. If required, in such cases, the court of
competent jurisdiction may be required to issue survey
commission as well. This exercise may not be done in the writ
petitions. Therefore, this Court does not see any reason to
make any interference. Accordingly, the writ petition deserves
to be dismissed at the stage of admission itself.

4
9. The petition is dismissed in limine.
